notice: RN bank batch 136: Maternity case studies: fetal monitoring on oxytocin, cord prolapse, preterm labor and the labor epidural. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require immediate action.

rationale.correct: Tachysystole with late decelerations and minimal variability is a Category II to III pattern.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues on the fetal monitor.

questions.stem: For each deceleration or pattern, indicate its usual cause (VEAL CHOP).

rationale.correct: VEAL CHOP links each pattern to a cause.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse's first action is to {{b1}}, because {{b2}}.

options.text: stop the oxytocin infusion
increase the oxytocin to speed birth
prepare for an epidural
perform a cervical exam
frequent strong contractions reduce placental blood flow
the cervix is not dilating
the client is tired
the FHR is normal

rationale.correct: Stop the oxytocin first.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Place the intrauterine resuscitation steps in order after stopping the oxytocin.

rationale.correct: Reposition, fluids, oxygen if needed, tocolytic if needed, then notify and document.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse calls the provider using SBAR. Which statements belong in the report? Select all that apply.

options.text: "Situation: recurrent late decelerations on oxytocin."
"Background: G1 at 41 weeks, induction, 5 cm."
"Assessment: tachysystole; oxytocin off, bolus given."
"Recommendation: please come to evaluate now."
"I think the baby is probably fine, so there is no rush to come."
"The resident ordered too much oxytocin again, like last week."

rationale.correct: SBAR gives a clear, factual report with a request.
references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: 10 minutes later
exhibits.body: Contractions 4 in 10 minutes. Late decelerations still present.

questions.stem: At 30 minutes, for each finding, indicate whether it shows recovery or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Recurrent late decelerations with absent variability

rationale.correct: Recovery allows the induction to restart carefully; absent variability with lates means emergency birth.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that show a cord prolapse emergency.

rationale.correct: Rupture with a high head and a cord in the vagina is prolapse.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each factor, indicate whether it raises the risk of cord prolapse.

rows.text: Rupture of membranes with an unengaged head

rationale.correct: An unengaged or small presenting part allows the cord to slip.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse's first action is to {{b1}}, while {{b2}}.

options.text: lift the presenting part off the cord with a gloved hand
push the cord back into the uterus
leave the room to call for help
start oxytocin
calling for help and preparing for emergency cesarean
waiting for full dilation
documenting the event first
removing the hand to check the FHR

rationale.correct: Relieve compression and prepare for immediate birth.

perOption.b1:b: Causes spasm and is not done.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which other actions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Knee-chest or steep Trendelenburg position
Cover exposed cord with warm moist gauze
Fill the bladder with saline if ordered
Keep the hand in place until birth
Massage the cord gently to restore its pulsation
Ask the client to push hard with the next contraction

rationale.correct: Positioning, cord protection and continued elevation.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The RN keeps the presenting part elevated. Which tasks can be given to other staff? Select all that apply.

options.text: Another RN: monitor the fetal heart rate and maternal vital signs
UAP: bring the warm saline and the emergency cart
UAP: call the operating room team using the emergency number
UAP: remove the RN's hand so the RN can document
UAP: decide when to move the client to the operating room

rationale.correct: The RN stays; others help.
references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Transfer
exhibits.body: Moving to the operating room on the bed.

questions.stem: After an emergency cesarean, for each finding, indicate whether it is reassuring or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Newborn breathing room air at 1 hour
Client says, "Did I do something wrong?"
Newborn tremors and poor feeding at 6 hours

rationale.correct: Good recovery; emotional needs and newborn signs need follow-up.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that confirm preterm labor.

rationale.correct: Regular contractions with cervical change before 37 weeks is preterm labor.

Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each medicine, indicate its purpose in preterm labor.

rationale.correct: Each drug has a different role.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The main purpose of tocolysis is to {{b1}} so that {{b2}}.

options.text: delay birth for about 48 hours
prevent preterm birth until 40 weeks
treat the infection
dilate the cervix
betamethasone can work and the client can be moved to a center with a NICU
the client can go home
labor will never return
the baby gains weight

rationale.correct: Tocolysis buys 48 hours for steroids and transfer.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Magnesium sulfate 4 g IV loading dose over 20 minutes is ordered. The bag contains 4 g in 100 mL. At what rate should the nurse set the pump? Record your answer in mL/hr.

rationale.correct: 100 mL over 20 minutes = 100 / (20/60) = 300 mL/hr.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Magnesium 4 g IV over 20 minutes, then 1 g/hr. Betamethasone 12 mg IM. Nifedipine.

questions.stem: Two hours into magnesium, review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Stop the magnesium infusion
Notify the provider
Prepare calcium gluconate
Check a magnesium level
Increase the infusion to 2 g/hr
Encourage oral fluids to flush it out

rationale.correct: Absent reflexes, slow breathing and low output mean magnesium toxicity.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: After labor stops and the client goes home at 31 weeks, for each statement, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I'll come in for contractions more than 4 to 6 an hour."
"Fluid leaking or low back pain means I should call."
"Strict bed rest will keep the baby in."

rationale.correct: Warning signs and treating triggers.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each description, indicate the stage of labor.

rows.text: From full dilation to birth of the baby
From onset of labor to full dilation
From birth of the baby to delivery of the placenta
First 1 to 4 hours after the placenta

rationale.correct: Labor has four stages.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

options.text: turn the client to the left side
raise the head of the bed to 90 degrees
stop the epidural catheter and remove it
give oxytocin
give an IV fluid bolus and phenylephrine or ephedrine as prescribed
wait 30 minutes
give a diuretic
give naloxone

rationale.correct: Reposition, fluids and a vasopressor.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which parts of the plan should the nurse include for a client with an epidural? Select all that apply.

options.text: Blood pressure every 5 minutes after a dose and then per policy
Check the bladder; catheterize if distended
Turn side to side every hour
Fall precautions; no walking alone
Let the client walk to the bathroom alone
Keep the client flat on the back

rationale.correct: Monitoring, bladder care, position changes and fall safety.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: 10 minutes later
exhibits.body: BP 116/70 after left side, bolus and phenylephrine. FHR 135/min.

questions.stem: The client is fully dilated and the head is at +1. Which actions should the nurse take during the second stage? Select all that apply.

options.text: Coach pushing with contractions when the urge comes (laboring down)
Check the FHR after each contraction
Watch for bulging of the perineum and crowning
Tell the client to push continuously between contractions
Push hard on the top of the uterus to speed birth

rationale.correct: Supported pushing, monitoring and watching for crowning.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Take action in the second stage.

questions.stem: In the fourth stage, for each finding, indicate whether it is expected or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Fundus firm at the umbilicus, midline
Lochia rubra, one pad in an hour
Fundus boggy and 2 cm above the umbilicus, deviated right
Shaking chills with a normal temperature

rationale.correct: Firm fundus and normal lochia are expected; a boggy, deviated fundus needs action.

perOption.r5:c1: Epidural block should be wearing off.
perOption.r5:c2: Epidural block should be wearing off.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

exhibits.title: Labor and delivery, 41 weeks

rows.label: Decelerations

rows.label: Vaginal exam
cells: A pulsating cord felt in the vagina

exhibits.body: A 22-year-old client (G1 P0) at 29 weeks has low back ache and tightening every 6 minutes for 3 hours. The client had a urinary tract infection last week that was not treated.

caseStudies.title: Labor epidural with hypotension and the stages of labor

exhibits.title: Labor and delivery

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
